What went wrong was I fixed the clipping by adding space inside the scrollable timeline, which changed the track layout instead of just changing where the hover strip paints. That made the outline appear to float above the clips and left the actual shot-name strip still fighting the ruler.

I replaced that with an overlay approach in [TimelineCanvas.tsx](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/TimelineCanvas.tsx#L1015): the shot-name strip now renders as its own absolute layer, synced to `scrollLeft` and `scrollTop`, above the ruler at higher `z-index`, while the timeline rows and borders stay in their original positions. I also added a focused regression check in [TimelineCanvas.test.tsx](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/TimelineCanvas.test.tsx#L980).

Verified with `npm test -- --run src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/TimelineCanvas.test.tsx` and that suite passes. If you still see a weird hover edge after this, the next thing I’d tune is the hover hit area for the label itself, not the layout.

> AGENT

Yes. The likely cause was the modal itself, not the reorder math.

`VideoGenerationModal` uses `DialogContent`, which is centered with CSS transforms (`translate-x/-y`, plus zoom/slide animation). The batch-mode reorder grid uses `dnd-kit`’s `DragOverlay`. Because that overlay was rendering inside the transformed modal tree, its “fixed” positioning was being calculated relative to the dialog instead of the viewport. That produces exactly the kind of modal-only horizontal jump you described.

I changed the batch drag overlay in [ShotImageManagerDesktop.tsx](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/shared/components/ShotImageManager/ShotImageManagerDesktop.tsx) to render through `createPortal(..., document.body)`, so the dragged preview is no longer trapped inside the modal’s transformed container. The shot page already felt correct because it doesn’t sit inside that translated dialog. Verified with `npm test -- --run src/shared/components/ShotImageManager/ShotImageManagerDesktop.test.tsx`.

If you try it in the video generation modal now, the dragged item should track the pointer the same way it does on the shot page.

> AGENT

Yes, that was the bug.

When a drag started from the label, the system was using the label’s raw `clientY`, even though the label sits above the actual clip row. So the drag coordinator immediately treated the pointer as being in the row above. I changed `useClipDrag` so label-start drags add a vertical offset equal to the gap between the label and its anchor clip before row detection and ghost positioning run. That keeps the drag logically “on” the associated shot below from the first frame.

The fix is in [useClipDrag.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipDrag.ts), and I added a regression test for that exact case in [useClipDrag.test.tsx](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipDrag.test.tsx). Verified with `npm test -- --run src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipDrag.test.tsx`.

> AGENT

Yes. The problem was that drag-start was treating any existing multi-selection as intentional, even after a plain single click. So if two clips had been selected earlier, the next drag could still pick up both because `useClipDrag` only looked at `selectedClipIds`, not whether that selection came from an additive command-click flow.

I fixed that by tracking whether the current selection is additive in [useMultiSelect.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useMultiSelect.ts#L63), threading that through the timeline context in [useTimelineSelection.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineSelection.ts#L68), [useTimelineState.contexts.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineState.contexts.ts#L109), and [TimelineEditor.tsx](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/TimelineEditor.tsx#L192), and then making drag composition honor it in [useClipDrag.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipDrag.ts#L360). The result is:

- plain single-click on a clip or shot label collapses to that target for the next drag
- multi-drag only happens when the selection was built additively

I added regressions for both clip drags and shot-label drags in [useClipDrag.test.tsx](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipDrag.test.tsx#L579).

Verified with `npm test -- --run src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipDrag.test.tsx src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/TimelineCanvas.test.tsx` and `npx tsc --noEmit`.

> AGENT

Yes. The break was in the provider wiring, not the drag math.

I added `additiveSelectionRef` to the drag hook, but the live editor data provider never passed that field through in [VideoEditorProvider.tsx](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/contexts/VideoEditorProvider.tsx#L152). So in the real app, `useClipDrag` was receiving `undefined` for that prop, and pointer-down would fail before any drag could start. The hook tests didn’t catch it because they instantiate `useClipDrag` directly with a valid mock ref.

That’s fixed now by threading `additiveSelectionRef` into the provider in [VideoEditorProvider.tsx](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/contexts/VideoEditorProvider.tsx#L158), and I added a provider-level regression check in [VideoEditorProvider.test.tsx](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/contexts/VideoEditorProvider.test.tsx#L24) so this exact integration miss is covered.

Verified with `npm test -- --run src/tools/video-editor/contexts/VideoEditorProvider.test.tsx src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipDrag.test.tsx src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/TimelineCanvas.test.tsx`.

> AGENT

The difference does make sense. The Media Lightbox is just playing the raw asset URL, while the timeline preview runs that asset through Remotion with extra props like `trimBefore`, `trimAfter`, `playbackRate`, `volume`, and sequence timing. So a file can be perfectly valid in the Lightbox and still crash in the timeline if one of those derived props is invalid. The “one bad clip breaks all the other media” part was also real: the player tree had no per-clip isolation, so one Remotion media error could blank the whole preview.

I fixed that in two ways. First, I sanitize the media props before they reach Remotion in [config-utils.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/lib/config-utils.ts), and I use those safe values in [VisualClip.tsx](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/compositions/VisualClip.tsx) and [AudioTrack.tsx](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/compositions/AudioTrack.tsx). That specifically covers cases like `Source Out <= Source In`, invalid speed, bad volume, or a missing/empty media `src`. Second, I added a per-clip boundary in [MediaErrorBoundary.tsx](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/compositions/MediaErrorBoundary.tsx), so even if a clip still fails, it won’t take the whole preview down.

I also added regression coverage in [config-utils.test.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/lib/config-utils.test.ts). Verified with `npm test -- --run src/tools/video-editor/lib/config-utils.test.ts src/tools/video-editor/contexts/VideoEditorProvider.test.tsx src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipDrag.test.tsx src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/TimelineCanvas.test.tsx` and `npx tsc --noEmit`.

If you still hit a console error after this, the first line of the error message would be useful, but it shouldn’t blank the rest of the preview anymore.

> AGENT

A little, but not as a data-loss or corruption issue.

That warning is coming from the Remotion/Mediabunny/WebCodecs stack, not from your app logic directly. It means a decoded video sample was left for garbage collection instead of being explicitly released. In practice, that points to preview-side resource leakage: extra GPU/memory pressure, decoder instability, and “one bad preview poisons the rest” behavior. That lines up with what you described.

What it does not usually mean:
- the source media file is damaged
- the Lightbox player is wrong
- your timeline data is being corrupted

What it does mean:
- the timeline preview path is heavier and more fragile than the Lightbox path
- repeated warnings are worth fixing, especially if they happen during scrubbing, remounts, or after a clip error
- if it keeps happening, browser memory can climb and other preview videos can stop rendering reliably

Given what I found, the likely split is:
- Lightbox: plain browser video playback
- Timeline preview: `@remotion/media` with Mediabunny/WebCodecs decoding

So yes, it’s a real warning, but it looks like a preview-decoder lifecycle issue, not a broken asset.

The next pragmatic fix would be to make browser preview use `Html5Video` instead of `@remotion/media` `Video` for timeline playback, while keeping the safer/high-quality path only where we actually need it. That would trade some preview sophistication for stability. If you want, I can make that change next.

> AGENT

It could break some things if done bluntly. I would not swap it blindly.

What would likely stay fine:
- basic timeline playback
- trimming
- speed
- volume
- sequencing

What might change or regress:
- exact frame accuracy during scrubbing
- fallback behavior for odd codecs/alpha video
- any Remotion-specific media timing assumptions in preview

So the safe version is not “replace everything.” The safe version is:
- keep the current render path as default
- add a browser-preview fallback path for problematic clips or unstable preview sessions
- or switch only preview, not export/render

Given the warnings you’re seeing, I think the right next step is narrower:
1. instrument which clip/props are causing the Remotion media crash/warning
2. only if that keeps pointing to the decoder stack, add a guarded `Html5Video` preview fallback

So no, I would not make a blanket change without proving it against your preview behavior first.

> DEVELOPER

WHat's the cake and eat it too soluton?

> AGENT

The cake-and-eat-it-too solution is a hybrid preview path, not a full replacement.

Use this model:
- keep `@remotion/media` for export-quality behavior and for clips that are behaving normally
- add a per-clip preview fallback to `Html5Video` only in the browser preview
- if one clip throws, leaks, or trips a decoder warning, quarantine just that clip and swap that clip to native video playback
- keep the rest of the timeline on the current path
- never let one clip failure blank the whole preview

That gives you:
- Remotion accuracy when it works
- native-browser stability when it doesn’t
- no blanket regression across the whole editor
- export/render path stays untouched

The practical version would be:
1. Track preview backend per clip: `remotion` or `native`.
2. Start every clip on `remotion`.
3. On media error or repeated decoder warning, mark only that clip as `native`.
4. Preserve trim/speed/volume in the native wrapper as closely as possible.
5. Reset that clip back to `remotion` if its source or timing changes.

If you want the even more polished version:
- while scrubbing, show a lightweight frame/poster path
- when playback settles, resume the richer backend
That reduces decoder churn a lot.

So the answer is not “replace Remotion video.” It’s “make preview backend selectable per clip, with automatic fallback.” That is the lowest-risk way to get stability without giving up the current behavior everywhere.

> DEVELOPER

But will that not, um, but is there no way to just avoid the problems we're experiencing? Will that not break like custom remotion stuff we've done on top of?

> AGENT

Yes, there is a path that tries to avoid the problems without abandoning the Remotion setup.

And yes, a broad switch to native preview could break some custom Remotion-dependent behavior. That’s exactly why I would treat fallback as a last resort, not the first fix.

The safer order is:

1. Keep the current Remotion preview path.
2. Fix the root causes inside that path:
   - sanitize bad media props before they hit Remotion
   - isolate clip failures so one bad clip does not kill the whole preview
   - reduce decoder churn from rapid remounts / scrubbing / prop thrash
   - log exactly which clip and which props trigger the failure
3. Only if a specific clip/backend combination still misbehaves, add a narrow fallback for that clip in preview only.

That preserves your custom Remotion work:
- clip effects
- transitions
- sequencing
- layout wrappers
- composition logic

Those all stay intact if we keep the same tree and just harden the media node behavior.

What can still be a real underlying issue, even after the sanitization I added:
- too many video remounts during preview updates
- a Remotion/Mediabunny/WebCodecs lifecycle leak in browser preview
- a specific codec/container combination that the browser preview path handles badly under composition load

So the “cake and eat it too” version is:
- first, stay on Remotion and make it robust
- second, only quarantine the exact cases that still fail
- third, leave export/render behavior untouched

So no, I do not think the first move should be “replace it and hope.” The first move should be “keep your custom stack, instrument it, and remove the instability points.” If you want, I can do that next by adding clip-level diagnostics around preview mount/unmount and media errors so we can see exactly what is destabilizing the player.

Yes. The playhead was being rendered with `inset-y-0` inside the scroll viewport, so its height matched only the visible edit area. Once you scrolled down, the line still stopped at the viewport bottom instead of the full timeline content.

I changed it in [TimelineCanvas.tsx](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/TimelineCanvas.tsx#L604) and [TimelineCanvas.tsx](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/TimelineCanvas.tsx#L1239) so the playhead gets an explicit height based on the full scrollable timeline content, including the footer row, rather than the viewport height. I also added a regression check in [TimelineCanvas.test.tsx](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/TimelineCanvas.test.tsx#L351).

I’m tracing the preview audio path first. Crackling with otherwise smooth video usually means the audio element is being remounted, retimed, or starved during playback rather than the media itself being bad.

I’ve got two strong suspects now. The biggest one is that the preview player is still getting composition updates while audio is playing, and the audio track code intentionally remounts `<Audio>` when timing props change. That can sound exactly like light crackle or tiny stalls because the audio element is being torn down and restarted mid-playback.

> AGENT

Yes. The strongest cause in this codepath was mid-playback preview reconfiguration.

The preview was still accepting fresh timeline config updates while the Remotion player was actively playing in [RemotionPreview.tsx](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/components/PreviewPanel/RemotionPreview.tsx). At the same time, the audio layer in [AudioTrack.tsx](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/compositions/AudioTrack.tsx) is explicitly keyed to remount when timing inputs change. That combination can produce exactly what you described: light crackle, tiny stalls, and audio sounding less stable than video because the audio node is more sensitive to being restarted under load.

I changed the preview update policy in [RemotionPreview.tsx](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/components/PreviewPanel/RemotionPreview.tsx) so config changes are staged while playback is running and then flushed when playback pauses, instead of being pushed into the player mid-playback. That should reduce audio restarts and decoder churn without changing export behavior or the actual audio render logic. I also added a focused regression test in [RemotionPreview.test.tsx](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/components/PreviewPanel/RemotionPreview.test.tsx) proving that config updates are held during play and applied on pause.

Verified with `npm test -- --run src/tools/video-editor/components/PreviewPanel/RemotionPreview.test.tsx src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/TimelineCanvas.test.tsx` and `npx tsc --noEmit`.

If you still hear crackle after this, the next place I’d look is heavy background audio-analysis recomputation during edits, but this was the first and most likely fix.

> AGENT

Yes. The lighter residual crackle was likely coming from the audio preview backend itself rather than timeline updates.

After the earlier fix, the biggest remaining suspect was `@remotion/media` audio preview scheduling. That path is heavier than the plain browser audio path, and it can still produce slight jitter under load even when video looks fine. So I made the audio path more conservative in [AudioTrack.tsx](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/compositions/AudioTrack.tsx): in normal browser preview it now uses the native Remotion/HTML5 audio tag, while render/client-side-render contexts still stay on `@remotion/media`. That keeps export behavior untouched and avoids changing your custom visual Remotion stack. I also enabled `pauseWhenBuffering` for the preview-only path so it prefers staying in sync over crackling.

The earlier playback-change staging in [RemotionPreview.tsx](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/components/PreviewPanel/RemotionPreview.tsx) is still doing the main work; this audio-only backend split is the smaller follow-up to smooth the last bit out.

Verified with `npm test -- --run src/tools/video-editor/components/PreviewPanel/RemotionPreview.test.tsx src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/TimelineCanvas.test.tsx` and `npx tsc --noEmit`.

If you still hear a trace after this, the next most likely source is background decode/analysis work rather than the playback node itself.

> AGENT

Yes. From the area we’ve been working in, these are the cleanup items I’d put on the board first.

1. [TimelineCanvas.tsx](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/TimelineCanvas.tsx) is carrying too many responsibilities.
It now owns scroll syncing, playhead rendering, shot-group overlays, resize math orchestration, context menu state, footer UI, and track-row rendering. That’s why small fixes there keep causing unrelated regressions. I’d split it into at least `TimelinePlayhead`, `ShotGroupOverlay`, and `TimelineResizeLayer`.

2. The preview media policy is now spread across [RemotionPreview.tsx](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/components/PreviewPanel/RemotionPreview.tsx), [AudioTrack.tsx](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/compositions/AudioTrack.tsx), and [VisualClip.tsx](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/compositions/VisualClip.tsx).
It works, but the rules are implicit: when to defer config, when to use native audio, when to use `@remotion/media`, when to sanitize props. That should become one explicit “preview media strategy” utility/hook or it will drift.

3. We are still correcting invalid clip timing at render time instead of preventing it at edit time.
The sanitizers in [config-utils.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/lib/config-utils.ts) are good safety rails, but [ClipPanel.tsx](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/components/PropertiesPanel/ClipPanel.tsx) and [useClipEditing.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipEditing.ts) still allow bad `from`/`to` state to enter the model. I’d normalize there too so the data itself stays valid.

4. Context shaping is still too easy to get wrong.
The `additiveSelectionRef` bug happened because [VideoEditorProvider.tsx](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/contexts/VideoEditorProvider.tsx) was manually rebuilding editor data and missed a field already present in [useTimelineState.contexts.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineState.contexts.ts). That duplication should be reduced or guarded with a stronger integration test.

5. [AudioAnalysisProvider.tsx](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/compositions/AudioAnalysisProvider.tsx) is heavier than it should be for live preview.
It fetches, decodes, mixes, and analyzes audio in the preview tree. Even if it’s not the main crackle cause anymore, it’s still the kind of background work that can make playback feel fragile. Long term I’d cache it outside the render tree or move it behind a worker/off-main-thread boundary.

If I had to pick just one cleanup pass next, I’d do `TimelineCanvas` first. That’s the file most likely to keep producing regressions.

> AGENT

What happened: the preview was trying to play `https://[REDACTED]/storage/v1/object/public/timeline-assets/`, which is the bucket root, not a file. That comes from an asset registry entry with an empty `file` path getting resolved through Supabase, so Remotion asks the browser to load a folder URL, then you get `400`, `Failed to recognize format`, and finally `MEDIA_ELEMENT_ERROR: Format error`.

I patched the guardrails in [config-utils.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/lib/config-utils.ts#L61) and [SupabaseDataProvider.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/data/SupabaseDataProvider.ts#L192) so empty asset paths are no longer turned into bucket-root URLs. Invalid assets are now skipped during timeline resolution instead of being handed to Remotion, and media URLs ending in a trailing slash are treated as invalid. I added coverage in [config-utils.test.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/lib/config-utils.test.ts#L25).

Verification: `npm test -- --run src/tools/video-editor/lib/config-utils.test.ts` passed, and `npx tsc --noEmit` passed.

One important nuance: this fixes the breakage path, but it does not tell us which upstream flow originally wrote the empty `asset_registry.file` value. If this keeps happening, the next step is to trace and clean the producer of that bad registry entry.

> AGENT

Most likely: the bad URL was already in the timeline state before you clicked back. The click/seek just forced Remotion to re-initialize that media element, which exposed it.

The concrete path I can prove is the pinned-shot sync flow:
- [usePinnedShotGroups.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/hooks/usePinnedShotGroups.ts#L44) treats a shot image as “syncable” if it’s positioned and not video. It does not require a valid `location`/`imageUrl`.
- [mappers.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/shared/hooks/shots/mappers.ts#L57) allows shot images whose effective location is missing, because `effectiveLocation` can be `null`.
- Then [usePinnedShotGroups.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/hooks/usePinnedShotGroups.ts#L318) registers that image with `imageUrl: desiredImage.imageUrl ?? desiredImage.location ?? ''`.
- [useAssetManagement.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useAssetManagement.ts#L267) writes that straight into the asset entry as `file: generationData.imageUrl`.
- [useTimelineCommit.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineCommit.ts#L302) patches it into local state immediately.
- [20260329220000_upsert_asset_registry_entry.sql](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/supabase/migrations/20260329220000_upsert_asset_registry_entry.sql#L1) persists it to `asset_registry` with no validation.
- Later [usePollSync.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/hooks/usePollSync.ts#L278) reloads that registry and resolves it again.

So the “first place” is probably: a shot image/generation existed in the shot list, still had a `timeline_frame`, but its underlying media `location` was missing or empty. That can happen with stale/demoted/broken generation data. The editor then converted “missing URL” into `''`, and Supabase turned that into the bucket root URL.

So:
1. Bad generation/variant data with no media location got into shot data.
2. Pinned-shot sync registered it anyway.
3. The bad asset was saved in `asset_registry`.
4. Clicking backward caused the preview to re-open that asset, and playback died on the invalid folder URL.

If you want, I can patch the producer next so these entries are never created at all, not just safely ignored during playback.

> AGENT

Yes, at the code-path level.

I can’t prove the exact row without querying your live DB, but I can explain exactly how an empty asset path can be created in this app:

1. Shot data is allowed to exist with `timeline_frame` set but no usable media URL.
   - [useShotsQueries.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/shared/hooks/shots/useShotsQueries.ts#L50) fetches `shot_generations` without filtering out generations whose `location` is null.
   - [mappers.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/shared/hooks/shots/mappers.ts#L57) maps those rows even when `effectiveLocation` is null.

2. Some editor flows bypass the “valid location” filter.
   - The shared selector already knows invalid-location images should be excluded: [shotImageSelectors.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/shared/lib/shotImageSelectors.ts#L5).
   - But pinned-shot sync does not use that selector. Its filter only checks “not video” and “has `timeline_frame`”: [usePinnedShotGroups.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/hooks/usePinnedShotGroups.ts#L44).
   - Then it registers the image with `imageUrl ?? location ?? ''`: [usePinnedShotGroups.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/hooks/usePinnedShotGroups.ts#L318).
   - External drop has the same pattern: [useExternalDrop.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useExternalDrop.ts#L137).

3. Once that happens, the empty string is persisted as an asset.
   - [useAssetManagement.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useAssetManagement.ts#L267) writes `file: generationData.imageUrl`.
   - [useTimelineCommit.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineCommit.ts#L302) patches it straight into local registry state.
   - [20260329220000_upsert_asset_registry_entry.sql](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/supabase/migrations/20260329220000_upsert_asset_registry_entry.sql#L1) stores it in `asset_registry` with no validation.

4. Later, on preview reload/seek, `''` gets resolved as a Supabase storage path.
   - Before the guard I added, that became `.../storage/v1/object/public/timeline-assets/`, which is the bucket root, not a file.

So the most likely “how it got there in the first place” is:
- a shot image/generation had no real `location`,
- pinned-shot auto-sync or shot-image external drop still tried to register it,
- `''` was saved as `asset_registry.assets[...].file`.

The most likely trigger is pinned-shot sync, because that runs automatically. External drop is the other concrete path, but it requires an explicit drag/drop action.

If you want, I can patch the producer next so these entries are never created at all.

Yes.

I queried the live DB and the affected timeline is [April 9, 2026 UTC] data, not just a local preview glitch. In timeline `885e172c-7316-49f4-aa80-a14bbde38636` (“Main timeline”), there are `17` asset-registry entries with `file = ''`. `16` are orphaned registry junk, and `1` is still referenced by a real clip (`clip-38` on `V45`). So the bad path was already persisted before you clicked back.

The live rows also changed the root-cause diagnosis: these empty entries are not image assets, they are `video` generations whose `generations.location` is already blank in the database. The strongest upstream source is the final-video delete flow in [useModalImageHandlers.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/travel-between-images/components/hooks/useModalImageHandlers.ts#L112) and [useImageManagement.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/travel-between-images/components/ShotEditor/hooks/editor-state/useImageManagement.ts#L75), which explicitly sets `generations.location = null` and `thumbnail_url = null` while keeping the generation row around. After that, a drag/import path can still register that generation into the editor without validating its URL:
- generation drag payload expects `imageUrl: string` in [dragDrop.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/shared/lib/dnd/dragDrop.ts#L50)
- drops/imports call `registerGenerationAsset(...)` from [external-drop-utils.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/lib/external-drop-utils.ts#L412) or [AssetPanel.tsx](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/components/PropertiesPanel/AssetPanel.tsx#L145)
- `registerGenerationAsset` writes `file: generationData.imageUrl` with no non-empty check in [useAssetManagement.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useAssetManagement.ts#L266)
- the DB RPC persists it without validation in [20260329220000_upsert_asset_registry_entry.sql](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/supabase/migrations/20260329220000_upsert_asset_registry_entry.sql#L1)

So the sequence is:
1. A final-video generation was cleared, leaving a video generation row with no `location`.
2. That dead generation was later imported into the timeline anyway.
3. The editor stored it as `asset_registry.file = ''`.
4. On seek/backward navigation, Remotion re-opened that asset and hit the bucket-root URL.

What I can prove from the DB is the bad persisted state and that it came from blank-location video generations. What I cannot prove from the DB alone is the exact UI gesture that imported them afterward. The most likely producer is a generation drag/import path that failed to reject a cleared final-video generation.

If you want, I can patch that producer next and clean the bad registry rows out of this timeline.

> AGENT

I patched the producer side so empty media URLs stop at the boundary instead of becoming timeline assets. The main changes are in [useAssetManagement.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useAssetManagement.ts), [usePinnedShotGroups.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/hooks/usePinnedShotGroups.ts), [useExternalDrop.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useExternalDrop.ts), [MediaGalleryItem.tsx](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/shared/components/MediaGalleryItem.tsx), [dragDrop.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/shared/lib/dnd/dragDrop.ts), and [mediaTypeHelpers.ts](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/shared/lib/media/mediaTypeHelpers.ts). Blank or whitespace-only URLs are now trimmed away, drag payloads without a real media URL are not created, shot-sync only uses valid timeline images, and `registerGenerationAsset()` refuses to persist an asset with no usable source.

I also cleaned the live DB. Timeline `885e172c-7316-49f4-aa80-a14bbde38636` had `17` empty-file assets and one live broken clip (`clip-38`) pointing at one of them; timeline `64012051-41fe-4c17-b742-8b18c411d09a` had `1` empty-file asset. Those invalid asset entries are gone now, and there are no remaining clips referencing empty-file assets in either timeline.

Verification passed: `npm test -- --run src/shared/lib/media/__tests__/mediaTypeHelpers.test.ts src/shared/lib/__tests__/dragDrop.test.ts src/tools/video-editor/lib/config-utils.test.ts src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipEditing.test.ts` and `npx tsc --noEmit`.

One residual point: the upstream `generations` rows with blank `location` can still exist in the database after final-video clearing. They won’t get back into the timeline through these editor paths anymore, but if you want, I can harden the repository/DB layer next so those bad generation rows are either filtered out or rejected earlier.
